patches printed as a readable list for each request.

request.description:
Fetches by id and writes safe patches back. Needs VNYX_API_TOKEN.
Keep HERMES_DRY_RUN=true until you trust the output.
Background sweep. Results land in logs/audit.jsonl, not the response.

Edit config/policy.yaml, hit this, no restart needed.
Use it to tune the grade bands while testing.

item.name: 10 - Readability: is the text in this photo legible?

formdata.description: Pick a photo of a care label or size tag. JPEG or PNG. Resize on the device first — 1280-1600px on the long edge at quality 80 is ~200KB and reads the same; a raw 12MP frame is 3-5MB and the upload alone blows the 1.5s budget.

OFF BY DEFAULT ON PURPOSE. The policy default is 1, and raising this is how you tell Hermes how much text to expect — but only raise it for a capture type you actually know. An adidas neck label carries 'adidas' and 'S' and nothing else, so min_lines=3 rejects a perfectly readable photograph of one. A full care label is the case where 4-6 is right.
OFF BY DEFAULT, same reasoning as min_lines. Policy default is 3.

request.description:
Can the text in this photograph be read, and if not, what should the operator change?

multipart/form-data, NOT base64 in JSON: base64 adds a third to the payload and upload is the largest item in the latency budget.

`readable` and `message` are the whole contract for a simple client. `reasons` carries a list, because a photo taken in a dark stockroom at arm's length is both underexposed and too far away.

START WITH THE OVERRIDES OFF. min_lines/min_chars are floors on how much text must be legible, and a floor above what the label actually carries rejects a good photograph — a two-line neck label cannot satisfy min_lines=3. Raise them only per capture type you know.

Watch `ocr_ms` and `duration_ms` in the response — they are how you tell whether the box is fast enough. See docs/READABILITY.md for the latency table and how to size it.
